Let me extract evidence from this T8 opinion piece.

Statements:

1. Stock fell below $200, down ~16% from highs, up 6% YTD — that's a share-price move; reject per instructions ("an investor's position or a share-price move").

2. "During its last quarterly conference call, management forecast that it expects hyperscaler spending to top $1 trillion in 2027 after reaching a projected $650 billion in 2026." — This is a company management statement (Nvidia management) about hyperscaler spending. It's a named party's claim/estimate → party_statement. Actually it's an aggregate industry quantity (hyperscaler capex) cited by Nvidia management. This is an industry aggregate for 2026/2027. Hmm — is it a candidate? "industry_aggregate: one aggregate quantity for one calendar year, such as the combined capital spending of named companies". Hyperscaler spending topping $1T in 2027, $650B in 2026 — that's an aggregate. Could propose as industry_aggregate candidate. But the guidance is Nvidia's own forecast of hyperscaler capex. Existing research group: ai-capex theme available as id "ai-capex". Hmm, but the candidate must have a settled_by public material: hyperscalers' reported capex in calendar 2026 aggregated by... hmm, settled by the sum of reported capex from the four major hyperscalers' annual filings. Feasible.

But careful: "the item's publication day 2026-07-06 falls in FY2027" — for calendar years use 2026. A candidate for 2026 hyperscaler capex = $650B? That's a numeric figure → 5 rungs. Due date: after Q4 2026 earnings, around 2027-02. Hmm, that's within 18 months? Due date for figures use publication date. Calendar year 2026 figures published in early 2027 — say 2027-02-15 or use annual reports. Let me set due_day 2027-02-28.

Actually should I use the 2027 $1 trillion? That's the more striking claim but 2027 calendar year ends after... due date would be ~2028-02, which is beyond? Not constrained by the 18-month rule (that applies to binding obligation yes/no events). Still, better to use 2026 to keep nearer term. Hmm. But the "current/next-year limit" for yearly metrics: "A yearly metric asks for a quantity over a defined fiscal or calendar period and keeps the current/next-year limit." Current year = 2026, next = 2027. 2026 hyperscaler capex is current year. Good.

3. "For the rest of this year, they expect 82% growth. For 2027, that figure rises to 41%." — Wall Street analysts projecting Nvidia revenue growth. third_party_view. These are analyst consensus estimates for Nvidia revenue growth. Could be evidence for a candidate on Nvidia revenue growth? Hmm, analyst growth estimates. Existing quantity: NVDA total_revenue. A candidate on FY2027 total revenue? The item gives growth rates, not a revenue figure. Could I propose a main_driver candidate on FY2027 revenue? Instructions: "main_driver: an annual quantity that carries the company's value (the segment that carries the business, gross margin, capital spending), whether or not the company guides it". Total revenue is certainly a main driver but is it "not every reported or guided line"? Total revenue is the core. Hmm, but a candidate thesis needs concrete rungs. We don't have revenue figures... we could construct rungs from growth rates implied. FY2026 revenue? Not given. Risky. Actually the growth rate figures themselves: 82% growth for "the rest of this year" (FY2027) and 41% for 2027 calendar. Hmm, "rest of this year" — the item was published July 2026, so "this year" likely calendar 2026 for revenue growth? Confusing. Analyst consensus for Nvidia: 82% growth for calendar 2026, 41% for 2027. Given NVDA FY2027 ends Jan 2027, calendar 2026 ≈ FY2027. I'd rather treat growth rate as evidence supporting a main_driver total revenue candidate... but that candidate would need rungs I can't ground.

Alternatively, propose a candidate on NVDA FY2028 EPS? Existing reference list doesn't include EPS measure. measure options include "other"? There's no EPS measure. Hmm. The item's central forecast: analyst average $12.76 EPS for FY2028; author thinks $300 by late 2027 using 25x. A candidate on FY2028 EPS would be measure "other" — but the schema's measure list lacks EPS. Could use "other" with unit USD. Hmm, that's allowed: measure enum includes "other", unit USD. But is EPS a "main_driver"? Earnings per share is not in the listed main drivers exactly, but "an annual quantity that carries the company's value" — EPS arguably. Hmm, risky.

I think the safest strong candidates:
- c1: Hyperscaler capital spending aggregate for calendar 2026 (industry_aggregate), theme "ai-capex". Rungs around $650B. Evidence: the management forecast. Also 2027 $1T as second evidence? Could link both evidence items if I split them. I might split the quote into one evidence item (single statement includes both years). Keep one evidence item.
- c2: NVDA FY2028 EPS consensus vs author's view? Hmm.

Let me consider a "demand" candidate: NVDA data center revenue? Not given. Skip.

period_start 2026-01-01, period_end 2026-12-31. due_day: 2027-02-28? Say 2027-02-15 — must be after all four report Q4 2026 results. Use 2027-02-28. Basis n/a, unit USD.

- c2: NVDA FY2027 total revenue growth rate, asset, main_driver, measure growth_rate, scope "total revenue". period_start 2026-02-01, period_end 2027-01-31. due_day 2027-02-28? Fiscal year note says FY2027's full-year figures are published in the annual report around 2027-02. Use 2027-02-28 as due date. year FY2027. Rungs percent: around 82. 
  r1 ≥90, r2 86–90, r3 78–86, r4 68–78, r5 <68. Hmm neutral should include 82 → 78-86 includes 82. Fine.

Wait — "For the rest of this year, they expect 82% growth. For 2027, that figure rises to 41%." The 82% for "rest of this year" — if this year = calendar 2026, then growth for full calendar 2026? Confusing wording. I'll frame the candidate as FY2027 revenue growth and note the analyst estimate of 82% for this year. Hmm, risk of misattribution. Actually maybe better frame the candidate as calendar 2026 revenue growth? NVDA doesn't report calendar years. Use FY2027 = period 2026-02 to 2027-01. Fine.

- c3: NVDA FY2028 EPS? Let's consider: analyst average $12.76 for FY2028. Author thinks conservative, implies $319 at 25x. But main_driver examples: "the segment that carries the business, gross margin, capital spending". EPS for FY2028 is a forecast beyond next-year? FY2028 is next year per fiscal note. Allowed.

Risk: is it too much? The instructions say open candidate only for the four reasons; "not every reported or guided line". I'll include two NVDA candidates? Maybe better to include just one to be safe... But the item's whole point is the $12.76 EPS → $319 thesis. I think EPS candidate is defensible as main_driver. However, measure "other" for EPS... hmm, "price" is an option but that's share price. There's no "eps". I'll use "other".

Hmm, alternatively skip c3 and just do c1 and c2. But then I lose the item's core. Let me think about which a careful analyst would flag.
